name: elemental_silicon

phase_0.boundary_condition: The diamond cubic crystal lattice surface where periodic boundary conditions close the infinite network into a finite computational cell.

⊢.justification: Before nucleation, silicon exists as disordered vapor atoms with no lattice structure — the void state prior to any covalent network formation.

⊣.justification: The fully formed diamond cubic lattice with periodic closure contains the entire system; no atom can leave without breaking the covalent network.

≻.justification: Atoms attach to the growth interface in a directed transformation, extending the tetrahedral network toward the target lattice configuration.

≺.justification: Heat drives a contravariant transformation where the ordered lattice descends into disordered liquid, reversing the growth morphism.

⋈.justification: Each new Si–Si bond composes with the existing network, chaining morphisms to extend the covalent structure one coordination shell at a time.

⊙.justification: A silicon atom in the lattice recognizes its fourfold coordination as its own identity — the local environment is the atom's self-reference.

∈.justification: The vapor-to-solid transition splits into two arms: crystalline ordering (T-arm) versus amorphous clustering (F-arm), each a distinct structural pathway.

∋.justification: Defects and disordered regions rejoin the perfect lattice through thermal annealing, fusing the divergent arms back into a single crystalline state.

⊤.justification: A successfully formed Si–Si bond at the correct tetrahedral angle deposits constructive truth — the affirmative arm of lattice formation.

⊥.justification: An unsatisfied valence or misoriented bond deposits constructive falsity — the negative arm where the lattice fails to close locally.

⊞.justification: At the melting point, crystalline and liquid phases coexist in a paradice — both ordered and disordered states held simultaneously without resolution.

⊡.justification: A vacancy or interstitial trapped during rapid quenching becomes a permanent, append-only record in the lattice that cannot be undone without melting.

phase_2.failure_reason: FSPLIT3 at step 3 dangles — no matching FFUSE3

phase_3.void_description: Disordered silicon vapor before any nucleation event — no bonds, no lattice, no structure.
phase_3.true_description: A fully coordinated silicon atom with four perfect tetrahedral bonds — the affirmative lattice site.
phase_3.false_description: A silicon atom with a dangling bond or wrong coordination — the negative defect site.
phase_3.both_description: A lattice region at the melting temperature where crystalline order and liquid disorder coexist in equilibrium — neither pure crystal nor pure liquid, both simultaneously held.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the domain with silicon vapor precursor — void state, no lattice exists.
Each vapor atom carries its intrinsic tetravalent identity — self-reference before bonding.
Nucleation bifurcation — vapor splits into crystalline nucleus arm and amorphous cluster arm.
Crystalline arm — directed growth front advances, adding atoms to the tetrahedral network.
Sequential bond formation on crystalline arm — each new Si–Si bond composes with the lattice.
Stable covalent bond formed at correct tetrahedral angle — deposits T on crystalline arm.
Newly bonded atom recognizes its fourfold coordination — self-reference in the lattice.
Continued lattice extension — composition chains the growth morphism across coordination shells.
Another successful bond — crystalline arm accumulates affirmative deposits.
Amorphous arm — thermal fluctuations drive descent into disordered clustering.
Dangling bond or miscoordinated site — deposits F on amorphous arm.
Amorphous cluster grows by disordered attachment — composition without tetrahedral order.
Another defect site — amorphous arm accumulates negative deposits.
At melting temperature, crystalline and amorphous regions coexist — paradice state held.
Annealing recombination — thermal energy allows amorphous regions to rejoin crystalline lattice.
Rejoined atoms recognize restored tetrahedral coordination — self-reference recovered.
Defect healed, perfect bond restored — affirmative deposit after fusion.
Growth resumes on unified lattice — forward morphism continues from fused state.
Lattice extends to macroscopic scale — sequential composition across the crystal.
High kinetic barrier — the strong covalent network freezes the structure at standard conditions.
Global correlation split — long-range elastic and electronic propagation spans the entire macroscopic lattice.
Conjunctive coordination — each atom simultaneously engages four neighbors to satisfy valence.
Subcritical phase — stable diamond cubic well away from any critical threshold.
Achiral lattice — inversion symmetry and mirror planes, no persistent orientational symmetry breaking.
Bond formation mechanism — strong covalent bonds create the tetrahedral network solid.
Non-polar interface — no directional preference at the covalent bond interface.
High fidelity — precise tetrahedral geometry enforces near-certain atomic interactions.
Higher-order symmetric participation — each atom symmetrically coordinates with four identical neighbors.
No topological protection — structure can melt or transform without crossing a topological boundary.
Completed crystal boundary — periodic closure contains the infinite network in a finite cell.
Frozen-in point defect recorded — permanent append-only mark in the lattice from quenching.
Another defect frozen — distinct irreversible record event in the crystal history.
Final self-reference — the lattice as a whole recognizes its own completed structure.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Quantum mechanical Hamiltonian translating atomic potentials into covalent bond formation rules.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Phonon-mediated elastic waves and electron-hole pair propagation across the lattice.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Crystal lattice itself — atomic positions encode state; defects are stored records.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Thermodynamic driving forces (chemical potential, temperature) determining growth vs. melting order.
phase_5.alfs_store: The diamond cubic unit cell — canonical reference structure for all silicon lattice operations.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Latent heat of fusion (50.55 kJ/mol) consumed per melting/solidification cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Ordered diamond cubic lattice at low temperature — low configurational entropy.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Disordered liquid silicon at high temperature — high configurational entropy.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The cycle is entropy-conservative when including the thermal reservoir; the lattice's information content is preserved in the periodic structure across phase transitions.
